name: James Lankford
signature: Kids-online-safety and chatbot guardrails cosponsor (KOSA, GUARD Act, NO FAKES) who also pushes bans on Chinese apps; quiet on data centers and state-law preemption.

notable_quote.text: AI chatbots with no safeguards pose real harm to our children. Parents should not have to wonder whether a digital tool in their home is manipulating or endangering their kids.

data_centers.summary: No public statements found on data centers as of Sept 2026. I searched his press releases, Oklahoma outlets and national news for data centers, electricity bills and ratepayers; his 2025 and 2026 permitting-reform releases exist but the pages were blocked and no data center mention surfaced in any headline or summary.

ai_risk.summary: Backs targeted AI guardrails: he cosponsors the GUARD Act to keep kids away from AI companion chatbots and the NO FAKES Act on AI voice and face copies, wrote a 2023 bill requiring agencies to disclose when AI makes decisions about people, and has pressed tech firms on deepfakes and watermarking. He has not called for broad licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Press release (Hawley): Lankford joins GUARD Act as cosponsor with statement on AI chatbots and children
evidence.quote: AI chatbots with no safeguards pose real harm to our children. Parents should not have to wonder whether a digital tool in their home is manipulating or endangering their kids
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants binding safety standards on AI chatbot companies where minors are concerned.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (age checks, no AI companions for minors)
evidence.what_it_shows: Formal cosponsorship of a bill imposing rules on AI chatbot companies.

evidence.title: S.1367 NO FAKES Act of 2025 (right to stop AI copies of voice or face)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal legal right against unauthorized AI deepfakes of a person.

evidence.title: S.4591 NO FAKES Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Re-upped support for the deepfake likeness bill in 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Lankford Wants Transparency When the Federal Government Uses AI to Interact with You (bill with Peters and Braun)
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is a powerful tool to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of our federal government, but we must always keep security, privacy, and any unintended consequences in mind before we turn any process or decision over to a computer
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants notice, human review and appeals when government AI makes decisions about people, a transparency-style guardrail.

evidence.title: Senate Intelligence hearing on the national security implications of AI (transcript): Lankford asks about watermarking on open platforms
evidence.what_it_shows: He raised how watermarking of AI content can work when open-source models are involved, showing interest in content-authenticity guardrails.

evidence.title: Press release: Senator Lankford Questions Social Media Executives During Senate Intel Hearing (deepfakes)
evidence.quote: the possibility and now the opportunity to be able to create video that looks strikingly real but none of it is actually real, all of it is computer generated
evidence.what_it_shows: Early concern about deepfakes and pressure on platforms to police them.

evidence.title: Press release (title only, page blocked): ICYMI: Lankford Raises Concerns on AI Scams, Fentanyl, and Terror Financing at Worldwide Threats Hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Per the title in his site index (archived April 2026) he raised AI-enabled scams as a threat at the 2026 Worldwide Threats hearing; the page itself could not be opened, so no detail is claimed.

tech_regulation.summary: Consistently backs targeted rules on tech platforms, especially for kids: cosponsor of the Kids Online Safety Act in both Congresses, STOP CSAM, SCREEN Act and the REPORT Act (now law), and he has asked the White House to ban the Chinese app WeChat. He attacks Big Tech over child safety and censorship but has not pushed break-ups or Section 230 repeal.

evidence.title: Press release: Lankford Celebrates Senate Passage of the Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: Social media companies designed their platforms to addict vulnerable younger users and enable sexual exploitation, harassment, enticement, and drug sales with minimal accountability for the poison and illegal activities on their platforms.
evidence.what_it_shows: Strong language holding social media companies accountable and backing a binding kids safety law.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsor of the main kids online safety bill.

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue platforms that fail on child abuse material.

evidence.title: S.737 SCREEN Act (age verification for adult sites)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports mandatory age checks on adult websites.

evidence.title: S.1409 Kids Online Safety Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Long-running support for KOSA.

evidence.title: S.474 REPORT Act (118th; became law)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a platform reporting mandate on child abuse material that became law.

evidence.title: Free Beacon: Lankford letter asks Trump to designate WeChat under the foreign adversary apps law and ban it
evidence.quote: would advance U.S. national security interests, protect American citizens from foreign criminals operating inside our borders, and help our law enforcement fight against Chinese criminal networks operating in my state and across the country
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants the government to use the TikTok-era law to ban a specific Chinese-owned app, a targeted intervention against a tech platform.

preemption.summary: No public position found on federal preemption of state AI laws. He voted with 98 other senators to strip the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 in July 2025, but that near-unanimous vote does not show a view either way, and I found no statement, letter or bill from him on the Dec 2025 executive order, the March 2026 White House framework or the state-preemption bills.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Lankford: Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to remove the moratorium, as did 99 of 100 senators after the deal collapsed; on its own this is not evidence he opposes preemption.

china_chips.summary: Leans hawkish on letting China access American AI: at a 2023 Intelligence hearing he pushed back on the idea that open research partnerships with Chinese firms are harmless, and in Jan 2026 he signed a letter asking the Energy Department to bar Chinese nationals from national labs working on the Genesis Mission AI platform. I found no statement on Nvidia chip sales or export control bills specifically.

evidence.title: Senate Intelligence hearing transcript: Lankford questions Meta and Alibaba ties and US-China AI research partnerships
evidence.quote: The challenge that we have with the AI side is we're in the process of still developing in so many areas when you form a partnership, then they're getting it near simultaneous.
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejected the argument that relaxed controls and open partnerships with China are fine for AI, a hawkish signal on technology transfer.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Cotton-led letter (Lankford signer) urges DOE to bar Chinese nationals from national labs amid the Genesis Mission AI effort
evidence.quote: prohibiting the national laboratories from granting Chinese nationals access to any national laboratory site, information, or technology
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to wall off US AI and energy research from Chinese access, consistent with a tighter-controls posture.

search_notes: Searches: 'James Lankford' + artificial intelligence, AI, data center, chatbot/deepfake/GUARD/NO FAKES, Big Tech/Section 230/KOSA, Nvidia/export controls/chips, preemption/moratorium, TikTok/AI executive order, WeChat, AI scams hearing, AI national security; site listing of lankford.senate.gov (about 80 archived tech/energy URLs). Opened: KOSA passage release, 2023 AI transparency bill release, 2018 Intel hearing release, Hawley GUARD Act release, TechPolicy.Press 2023 hearing transcript, MeriTalk Cotton letter, Free Beacon WeChat letter, govtrack s363. Blocked (403 direct, Wayback connection refused for most of the session): the 2026 'AI scams' Worldwide Threats release, the 2025 'Big Tech protecting child predators' bill release, the 2025-26 permitting releases, the CPAC Big Tech release, and the Ricketts 'stable regulatory environment to win the AI race' letter (could not confirm whether Lankford signed; treat as unverified). Google News URL decoder was rate-limited, so a News 9/News On 6 item on Lankford and the Trump-Xi summit (possible chips content) was not opened. No AI caucus membership or PAC activity found.

name: Alan Armstrong
signature: Ex-Williams CEO appointed to the Senate in March 2026 who made permitting reform for AI-era power demand his signature issue (American Energy and Mineral Infrastructure Act).

notable_quote.text: The United States cannot pursue AI dominance, industrial reshoring, advanced manufacturing growth, and long-term energy reliability while tolerating a permitting regime that is fertile ground for procedural obstruction and endless litigation.

data_centers.summary: Build faster. He argues AI and data centers are driving a power surge the grid cannot meet, blames permitting delays and interconnection backlogs for pushing data centers behind the meter, calls opposition to data centers NIMBYism, and has introduced a sweeping permitting bill. He frames delay, not data centers, as what raises consumer bills.

evidence.title: Op-ed (Washington Reporter): The same permit snare that stops pipelines will stop the grid buildout too
evidence.quote: As artificial intelligence takes flight, cloud-based data management continue to grow, manufacturing returns to our shores, and technology in general demands more and more 24/7 power, the demands on our strained grid is surging.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI-driven power demand as a reason to build transmission faster and reform Clean Water Act Section 401 reviews.

evidence.title: Op-ed in 535 News (reprinted by OK Energy Today): America built the 20th century. Can we build the 21st?
evidence.quote: Under the current system, large power consumers like major industrial players and data center developers are increasingly bypassing the public grid entirely, building private "behind-the-meter" energy systems because public infrastructure cannot keep pace.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants faster grid and generation buildout so data centers can connect, citing 8 to 15 year interconnection studies and China outbuilding the US.

evidence.title: Columbia Energy Exchange podcast transcript: Armstrong says AI and data centers cannot be divorced from permitting reform, calls data center opposition NIMBY
evidence.quote: It's interesting to me how many people want to see those two things divorced. And I don't think they are divorced practically.
evidence.what_it_shows: He links the data center boom directly to his permitting push and criticizes groups that fight data centers.

evidence.title: Broadband Breakfast: Energy permitting delays threaten US AI growth, Armstrong says at US Energy Association event
evidence.quote: What we don't have is a permitting process that allows us to get the infrastructure built
evidence.what_it_shows: He tied permitting reform to rising AI electricity demand and competing with China, and wants concurrent agency reviews and tougher standards for courts to block projects.

evidence.title: OK Energy Today: Armstrong introduced the American Energy and Mineral Infrastructure (AEMI) Act and is building support for it
evidence.what_it_shows: His first Senate bill is a comprehensive permitting overhaul backed by energy, mining, utility and infrastructure groups, aimed at getting AI-era power projects built.

ai_risk.summary: No public position found on regulating AI itself. His AI comments are about powering the AI boom and beating China on infrastructure, not about safety rules, chatbots or liability. I searched his op-eds, speeches, podcast and news coverage since his March 2026 appointment.

tech_regulation.summary: Thin record pointing to targeted rules: since joining the Senate he cosponsored the STOP CSAM Act (platform accountability for child abuse material) and the Connected Vehicle Security Act (banning Chinese-linked car software). No statements on Big Tech, Section 230 or privacy found.

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making platforms do more on child sexual abuse material and letting victims sue.

evidence.title: S.4429 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a ban on connected-car software and parts from China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

preemption.summary: No public position found. He was not in the Senate for the July 2025 moratorium vote and I found no statement on state AI laws, the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

china_chips.summary: No position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. He often says China is outbuilding US power capacity and cosponsored a bill banning Chinese-linked connected-car technology, but nothing on semiconductors.

search_notes: Searches: 'Alan Armstrong' senator + artificial intelligence, data center, AI China chips regulation, Google/Stillwater/ratepayers, kids/STOP CSAM/Big Tech/TikTok, AI hearing/HELP/jobs, Sen. Alan Armstrong + China/chips/Nvidia; site listing of armstrong.senate.gov returned zero archived URLs and both direct and WebFetch attempts on the site were 403. Opened: Broadband Breakfast (May 12), Washington Reporter op-ed (Jun 16), OK Energy Today (Aug 5 and Aug 31, which reprints his 535 News op-ed in full), Columbia CGEP podcast transcript (Jul 28). Not opened (decoder rate-limited): Fox News, News 9, Washington Times and E&E pieces on his permitting push; they appear to repeat the same message. No PAC activity, caucus membership or leadership role found; he is a temporary appointee through the end of 2026.

name: Kevin Hern
signature: GOP Senate nominee backed by the Leading the Future super PAC who frames AI as a national security race with China and wants more power and permitting for data centers.

notable_quote.text: You can't have AI if you don't have energy to run the data centers. Small modular reactors are huge for AI and for our military bases.

groups: House Republican Policy Committee Chairman (119th Congress, through April 2026)

data_centers.summary: Build faster. In a Jan 2026 interview he said the country must have power for data centers, called for permitting reform and off-grid small modular reactors to run them, and complained that coal plants were retired while China adds them. No conditions or ratepayer concerns mentioned; based on one interview.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter interview: Hern on energy for AI data centers
evidence.quote: You can't have AI if you don't have energy to run the data centers. Small modular reactors are huge for AI and for our military bases.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants permitting reform and independent off-grid power so data centers can be built and run.

ai_risk.summary: Light touch, China first. Asked whether he would back a bill preempting state AI laws paired with kids protections, he answered that AI is a national security matter and the US must stay the leader over China; he did not raise safety rules. The pro-industry Leading the Future super PAC endorsed him and pledged $850,000 for his Senate race.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter interview: Hern on AI as a national security race with China
evidence.quote: This isn't something that we're experimenting with; this is really a national security thing. China is doing AI, and we need to do the same thing.
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI frame is winning the race with China, an innovation-first posture rather than new safety mandates.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter: Leading the Future to spend $850,000 backing Hern's Senate bid
evidence.quote: Leading the Future also told the Reporter that it will be spending $850,000 backing Hern in his Senate race.
evidence.what_it_shows: The industry-funded pro-innovation super PAC, which wants a national AI framework, is investing heavily in him.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future's second slate of House GOP endorsements includes Hern
evidence.what_it_shows: Formal endorsement by the pro-AI-industry super PAC alongside Scalise, Guthrie and other leadership figures.

tech_regulation.summary: Only a China-focused record: he cosponsored the 2024 law forcing TikTok's sale or ban and, as RSC chairman, pushed the Counter Communist China Act on Chinese investment. No statements found on Big Tech, Section 230, privacy or kids online safety.

evidence.title: H.R.7521 Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (118th; TikTok divest-or-ban law)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed forcing a foreign-adversary-controlled app off US app stores.

evidence.title: Hudson Institute event: Taking On the China Challenge with Congressman Kevin Hern (transcript; RSC Counter Communist China Act)
evidence.what_it_shows: He cited TikTok as one example of Chinese influence Congress must address and promoted a bill regulating Chinese investment.

preemption.summary: No clear position. When a reporter asked directly whether he would support preempting state AI laws if paired with the Kids Online Safety Act, he pivoted to China and national security without answering. His main super PAC backer wants a national framework, but that is the PAC's view, not his stated one.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter interview: Hern asked about preempting state AI laws with KOSA
evidence.what_it_shows: He was asked the preemption question directly and did not take a position, answering instead about the AI race with China.

china_chips.summary: Leans hawkish on technology flows to China: at Hudson in 2024 he called for scrutiny of outbound US investment in Chinese chip, 5G and aerospace development and said a technology war is under way. He opposed the 2022 CHIPS Act as wasteful spending, which is about subsidies, not export controls. Nothing found on Nvidia H20/H200 sales or the Chip Security Act.

evidence.title: Hudson Institute event transcript: Hern on outbound investment in Chinese chip development
evidence.quote: when we look at outbound investments from the United States and we look at the tremendous growth in certain sectors, especially when it comes to national defense areas, areas of technology, whether it be aerospace or 5G, or chip development
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to restrict American money flowing into Chinese chip and defense technology.

evidence.title: Press release: 'Now is the time to fight': Hern argues against CHIPS, BBB (House floor speech)
evidence.quote: urging his colleagues to vote against the Democrats' CHIPS bill, a gateway to their revived Build Back Broke plan
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed the semiconductor subsidy law on spending grounds; a mixed data point, not a view on export controls.

search_notes: Searches: 'Kevin Hern' + artificial intelligence, data center, Leading the Future, AI Senate Oklahoma, Big Tech/Section 230/chips/Nvidia/export controls, national framework/preemption/chatbot, Public First/Defending Our Values, Policy Committee AI, campaign AI; hern.house.gov press listings for 2022, 2025 and 2026 read. Opened: Washington Reporter Jan 20 2026 interview (full transcript section), Washington Reporter Jun 2 2026 LTF story, Breitbart May 22 2026, Hudson Institute Mar 2024 transcript, Hern 2022 CHIPS floor speech release. Unverified leads: the landscape file says Public First's Defending Our Values PAC spent about $808,000 supporting Hern (May-Jun 2026) and American Mission spent about $253,000; the Transformer tracker page is JavaScript-only and the FEC API DEMO_KEY was rate-limited, so I could not open a source and did not include it as evidence. AEI's Dec 5 2025 'AI Governance' event with Obernolte featuring Hern was 403 on both fetchers. Hern's House site shows he chaired the House Republican Policy Committee until April 15 2026 and the RSC in the 118th Congress.

name: Josh Brecheen
signature: Homeland Security oversight subcommittee chairman focused on AI-enabled cyberattacks from China; on data centers he wants transparency about electricity costs but says Congress should not build a regulatory regime.

notable_quote.text: Congress is not gonna create the regulatory environment. What we can do is make sure people have information about the data centers.

groups: Chairman, House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Accountability

data_centers.summary: Mixed. At an Aug 2026 McAlester town hall about the IREN data center near Kiowa he said operators must not drive up people's electricity costs and pointed to a bill he cosponsors requiring the Energy Department to report data center power and water use, but he added Congress will not create a regulatory regime and should only provide information.

evidence.title: KJRH: Brecheen gives views on data centers, smelter, election denial in McAlester (town hall remarks)
evidence.quote: have to make sure that they are not driving up people's electricity costs
evidence.what_it_shows: He voices the ratepayer concern about data centers while rejecting federal regulation, favoring disclosure instead.

evidence.title: H.R.9019 POWER Act (Roy): Energy Department reporting on data center electricity and water use
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsorship confirmed in the official bill status file; a transparency measure, not a limit on building.

ai_risk.summary: Mixed. As subcommittee chairman he held a Dec 2025 hearing with Anthropic and Google on an AI-driven cyberattack, said AI-enabled attacks should concern all Americans and doubted company safeguards alone will stop misuse, but his remedy was stronger federal cyber defenses and information sharing, not rules on AI developers. He voted against the FY27 NDAA, which carried AI provisions, for reasons I could not document.

evidence.title: Homeland Security Committee release: Subcommittee Chairmen Ogles, Brecheen opening statements in hearing with Anthropic, Google, Quantum Xchange on the future of cybersecurity
evidence.quote: even if U.S.-based AI companies can put safeguards against using their models for cyberattacks, cyber threat actors will find other ways to access this technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI-powered hacking as a serious, growing threat but frames the answer as DHS defenses and public-private partnership rather than new AI regulation.

evidence.title: House roll call 278 (2026): passage of H.R. 8800, FY27 NDAA, which included the AGI Preparedness Initiative and AI incident reporting provisions (Brecheen: Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: One of seven Republicans voting no on the defense bill; his stated reasons were not found, so this is not treated as a position on the bill's AI sections.

tech_regulation.summary: Leans toward targeted rules on the kids side: he cosponsored the SCREEN Act in both Congresses to require age verification on adult websites. No statements found on Big Tech, Section 230 or privacy.

evidence.title: H.R.1623 SCREEN Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports mandatory age checks for adult websites.

evidence.title: H.R.6429 SCREEN Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier cosponsorship of the same age-verification bill.

preemption.summary: No public position found on federal preemption of state AI laws. I found no statement, letter or cosponsorship on the moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

china_chips.summary: No position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales. He is hawkish on Chinese state hacking (he co-signed a 2025 letter on the Volt and Salt Typhoon intrusions and calls China the top cyber threat), but nothing on semiconductors.

evidence.title: Homeland Security Committee release: Chairmen Green, Garbarino, Brecheen letter to DHS on China-backed Typhoon intrusions
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows China-hawk oversight on cyber intrusions, not a position on chip export policy.

Opened: KJRH Aug 28 2026 town hall story, govinfo bill status for H.R.9019 (confirms cosponsorship dated 2026-08-10), govtrack and clerk.house.gov for roll call 278, Homeland Security Committee search page and the Dec 17 2025 and Mar 17 2025 releases.
